title: How VoIP(Voice over Internet Protocol) Works
excerpt: If you’ve never heard of VoIP before, prepare to have your perspective on long-distance phone conversations shifted.
author: SipLink Team

children.text: If you’ve never heard of VoIP before, prepare to have your perspective on long-distance phone conversations shifted.
VoIP, or Voice over Internet Protocol, is a way of converting analogue audio signals, such as those heard when talking on the phone, into digital data that can be sent over the Internet.
What is the benefit of this? As a result, if you use some of the free VoIP software available to make Internet phone calls, you’ll be completely circumventing the phone company (and its expenses).
The wonderful thing about VoIP is that you can make a call in a variety of ways. Today, there are three distinct “flavours” of VoIP service in widespread use:

ATA – The most straightforward and usual method is to use an ATA device (analog telephone adaptor). The ATA allows you to use VoIP by connecting a regular phone to your computer or Internet connection. The ATA is a digital-to-analog converter. It converts the analogue signal from your standard phone into digital data that may be transmitted over the Internet. SIPLINK Communications, for example, offers free ATAs as part of their service. Simply take the ATA out of the package, put the cord from your phone into the ATA instead of the wall socket, and you’re ready to make VoIP calls.

IP Phones – These specialty phones have a handset, cradle, and buttons, much like regular phones. The IP phones, on the other hand, have an RJ-45 Ethernet connector instead of the typical RJ-11 phone connector. IP phones connect directly to your router and come equipped with all of the required hardware and software to conduct IP calls. Subscribers of Wi-Fi phones can make VoIP calls from any Wi-Fi hotspot.

Computer-to-computer- This is without a doubt the most straightforward method of using VoIP. Long-distance calls are also free of charge. There are a number of companies that provide free or extremely low-cost software for this sort of VoIP. All you’ll need is the software, as well as a microphone, speakers, a sound card, and an Internet connection, preferably one that’s as fast as a cable or DSL modem. There is normally no payment for computer-to-computer conversations, regardless of distance, except from your regular monthly ISP fee.
Advantages of Using VoIP:

To provide phone service, VoIP technology makes use of the Internet’s packet-switching capabilities. Compared to circuit switching, VoIP provides in India a number of advantages. In a circuit-switched network, packet switching, for example, allows numerous telephone calls to share the same amount of space as one. That 10-minute phone call we mentioned previously took 10 minutes of transmission time on the PSTN at a rate of 128 Kbps.

That identical call might have taken only 3.5 minutes of transmission time at a cost of 64 Kbps. A leaving another 64 Kbps free for those 3.5 minutes, plus an additional 128 Kbps for the remaining 6.5 minutes. If VoIP had been used. According to this basic calculation, three or four additional calls may readily fit into the area occupied by a single call in the existing system. And this example ignores the use of data compression, which decreases the size of each call even more.
Disadvantages of Using VoIP:

The modern Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) is a reliable and nearly bulletproof system for making and receiving phone calls. We’ve all become accustomed to the fact that phones simply function. Computers, e-mail, and other connected technology, on the other hand, are still a little shaky. Let’s face it: when their e-mail goes down for 30 minutes, few people panic. A half-hour of no dial tone, on the other hand, can easily drive folks into a panic. So, whatever inefficiency the PSTN may have, it more than makes up for in dependability. However, the Internet’s network is significantly more complex, and as a result, it operates with a far larger margin of error. All of this adds up to one of VoIP’s key flaws: reliability.

title: IP-Enabled Services
excerpt: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) is a technology that allows you to make voice calls via the Internet rather than over a traditional (or analogue) phone line. Some VoIP services limit you to cal...
author: SipLink Team

children.text: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) is a technology that allows you to make voice calls via the Internet rather than over a traditional (or analogue) phone line. Some VoIP services limit you to calling only other VoIP users, while others allow you to call anyone with a phone number, including local, long-distance, mobile, and international lines. Additionally, while some VoIP services require you to use your computer or a specific VoIP phone, others enable you to use a regular phone with a VoIP adaptor.
FAQ for VoIP

VoIP services in india turn your voice into a digital signal that can be transmitted over the Internet. If you call a conventional phone number, the signal is transformed to a standard phone signal before it reaches the intended recipient. A computer, a dedicated VoIP phone, or a standard phone connected to a special adaptor can all be used to make a VoIP call. Furthermore, wireless “hot spots” in places like airports, parks, and cafés allow you to connect to the Internet and may even allow you to use VoIP services while on the go.
How VoIP / Internet Voice Works?
What kind of gear do I require?

It is necessary to have a broadband (high-speed Internet) connection. A cable modem, high-speed services like as DSL, or a local area network can all be used. It is necessary to have a computer, adaptor, or specialist phone. Some VoIP services can only be used with a computer or a special VoIP phone, while others can be used with a regular phone and a VoIP adaptor. You’ll need some software and a cheap microphone if you use your PC. Special VoIP phones link to your broadband connection and function similarly to standard phones. You’ll be able to dial exactly like you always have if you use a phone with a VoIP adaptor, and the service provider may also give additional features.
Is it possible to tell the difference between a local and a long-distance call?

Some VoIP companies give their services for free, but only for calls to other VoIP subscribers. You may be able to choose an area code other than the one in where you live if your VoIP provider allows it. It also means that depending on their area code and service, anyone who phone you may suffer long-distance charges.

Some VoIP companies, like traditional landline telephone service, charge for long distance calls to numbers outside your calling area. Other VoIP services allow you to call anywhere for a set number of minutes at a fixed charge.
If I have VoIP service, who can I call?

You may be limited to calling only other subscribers to the service, or you may be able to call anyone with a phone number, including local, long distance, mobile, and international numbers, depending on your subscription. If you call someone on a conventional analogue phone, they will not require any extra equipment to speak with you. Some VoIP services allow you to speak with multiple people at the same time.
What Are Some of the Benefits of VoIP?

Some VoIP services include features and services that are either not available with a traditional phone or are offered for a cost. You might be able to save money by not having to pay for both a broadband connection and a traditional phone line.
What are some of the drawbacks of VoIP?
If you’re thinking about switching from standard phone service to VoIP, there are a few things to consider:
During power outages, some VoIP services may not work, and the service provider may not provide backup power.
Not all VoIP providers use 9-1-1 to connect to emergency services. See VoIP & 911 Advisory for more details.
Directory assistance/white page listings may or may not be available from VoIP providers.
When I travel, can I bring my phone adapter with me?

Some VoIP service providers provide services that can be used everywhere there is access to a high-speed Internet connection. Using a VoIP service from a different location may affect your ability to call 9-1-1 for emergency assistance. See VoIP & 911 Advisory for more details.
Is it necessary for my computer to be turned on?
Only if your service requires you to use your computer to make calls. Your broadband Internet connection is required for all VoIP services.
How can I tell whether I’m on a VoIP call ?

The phone will ring like a traditional phone whether you have a specific VoIP phone or a standard phone linked to a VoIP adaptor. If your VoIP service requires you to make calls using your computer, your service provider’s software will notify you when a call comes in.
Does the FCC Regulate VoIP?

The FCC imposed 911 responsibilities on providers of interconnected VoIP services, which allow customers to make and receive calls over the normal telephone network, in June 2005. You should be aware, however, that 911 calls made using VoIP are handled differently than 911 calls made through a traditional phone line. For more information on the differences between VoIP and 911 services, please view our consumer fact sheet.

The FCC also requires interconnected VoIP providers to adhere to the Communications Assistance for Law Enforcement Act of 1994 (CALEA) and contribute to the Universal Service Fund, which supports communications services in high-cost areas and for income-eligible telephone consumers. With new improvements in internet technology, some of these factors may change. Always double-check with the VoIP service provider you choose to confirm any benefits and limits of their service.
